title_en: Trump makes Alaska the latest frontier in his election power grab
title_zh: 特朗普让阿拉斯加成为他争夺选举权力的最新前沿
summary: The move by the Justice Department to try and preemptively block Alaska’s Senate results if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses stunned officials in both parties.
summary_zh: 如果共和党参议员丹·沙利文在博茨瓦纳选举中落败，司法部将试图先发制人地阻止阿拉斯加州参议院的选举结果，这让官员们感到震惊
body_en: President Donald Trump is escalating his crusade to exert control of America’s elections as his party barrels towards a potentially bruising midterm.

The Justice Department has already filed lawsuits in nearly every state to try and gain access to voter files. Trump revisited his longstanding bid to restrict mail voting, sparking a legal battle that reached the Supreme Court. He sought to make anti-terrorism funds for state and local governments contingent on how they administer elections. He has threatened to withhold federal election funding from states that refuse to change voter registration forms and sparred with Republican lawmakers over a bill to overhaul elections.

But with most of those efforts stalling, on Thursday, just 12 days before Election Day, the DOJ took things even further: In an extraordinary move, it asked a court to preemptively block Alaska’s Senate results if Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan loses, stunning current and former election officials in both parties.

“Boy, they are scraping the bottom of the barrel. It feels like a real desperation play to me, because it has got zero basis in the law,” said Ben Ginsberg, a veteran Republican election law expert who was counsel to George W. Bush’s 2000 and 2004 presidential campaigns.

At virtually every corner, courts have rebuffed Trump’s efforts, and legal experts expect the latest DOJ maneuver to have the same outcome. The requests for voter rolls were blocked repeatedly by members of Trump’s own party and struck down in court . The attempt to restrict mail voting was ultimately blocked by the Supreme Court. Federal judges blocked both the anti-terrorism and election funding efforts. The SAVE Act, which would require voters to provide proof of citizenship at the polls, has stalled in the Senate.
But Trump keeps pushing, telling reporters Friday that he had personally green-lit the Alaska lawsuit: “I'm the one that said 'Do it.’”
The gambit is another sign that Trump is once again ramping up his efforts to exert greater control over how elections are administered — with officials bracing for what may come next.

“I think there is an attempt to lay a foundation to say, ‘If we had won these lawsuits, we would have won the election,’” Gabriel Sterling, a Republican and former senior Georgia elections official who sparred with Trump over his false claims of fraud in the state in 2020, said of the Alaska lawsuit. “So, for them, filing and losing for them is the same difference, tactically speaking, potentially.”

Trump has been claiming elections were being stolen from him since the 2016 primaries , and his wide-ranging legal and political attempts to overturn his 2020 election loss sparked a riot at the U.S. Capitol in January 2021, even as some in his party want him to move on .

“The federal government is his company, and he gets to call all the shots of his company, and that's just never how it's been done before,” said Stephen Richer, Maricopa County, Arizona’s former GOP chief election official.

POLITICO reached out to the offices of every Republican statewide election official in America for a response to the DOJ’s action in Alaska. Four declined to comment, and the rest did not respond. Their silence shows just how powerful Trump remains in the party, and how few are willing to cross him just days before November’s midterms.

"The survival rate politically of people who oppose Donald Trump on this issue is not great if you're Republican,” said Richer, who was ousted by a more conservative Republican in a 2024 primary after defending the county’s 2020 election results against a yearslong campaign from Trump and his allies to try to prove they were rigged .
Arizona Democratic Secretary of State Adrian Fontes railed against the DOJ’s lawsuit, accusing the department of “working as the president's lawyers.”

“The Department of Justice is acting in a monstrously political way, and it's purely inappropriate, and they lose a lot of credibility by putting their thumb on the scales,” Fontes said in an interview Friday afternoon. “This attempt in Alaska, if it comes to Arizona, will also fail.”

The Justice Department, in a statement posted on social media , said "claims that DOJ is trying to stop Alaska’s election are FALSE." Instead, the DOJ argued it was "seeking to protect election integrity, consistent with the National Voter Registration Act (enacted by Congress) and ensure the will of Alaska voters is respected."

Washington state Attorney General Nick Brown, a Democrat, described the legal filing in Alaska as “part of a concerted effort to control the election and to try to dictate the outcome in Donald Trump and the Republican Party’s favor.”
Brown said he worried the administration would contest the results of the midterms.

“That is not hypothetical,” Brown said. “This is what the president has done for years now, and he has the entire power of government, and most importantly, the Department of Justice around elections, acting at his request.”
Sterling predicted the effort would backfire on the GOP.

“By talking about stolen elections, by talking about cheating, they're suppressing their own vote and they're encouraging the votes of their opponents,” he said. “So tactically, I think it's politically moronic.”
body_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统正在升级他的十字军东征，以控制美国的选举，因为他的政党正朝着可能惨烈的中期选举迈进。
司法部已经在几乎每个州提起诉讼，试图获取选民档案。特朗普重新审视了他长期以来限制邮寄投票的主张，引发了一场法律战，并闹到了最高法院。他试图根据州和地方政府管理选举的方式为其提供反恐资金。他威胁要扣留那些拒绝改变选民登记表格的州的联邦选举资金，并与共和党议员就一项改革选举的法案发生争执。
但随着大部分努力陷入停滞，周四，距离选举日仅 12 天，美国司法部采取了更进一步的措施：采取一项非同寻常的举措，要求法院在共和党参议员丹·沙利文 (Dan Sullivan) 失败的情况下，先发制人地阻止阿拉斯加州参议院的选举结果，这令两党现任和前任选举官员感到震惊。
“天哪，他们正在彻底解决问题。对我来说，这真是一场绝望的游戏，因为它的法律基础为零，”曾担任乔治·W·布什 (George W. Bush) 2000 年和 2004 年总统竞选顾问的资深共和党选举法专家本·金斯伯格 (Ben Ginsberg) 说。
几乎在每个角落，法院都拒绝了特朗普的努力，法律专家预计司法部的最新举措也会产生同样的结果。选民登记的请求多次遭到特朗普所在政党成员的阻止，并在法庭上被驳回。限制邮寄投票的尝试最终被最高法院阻止。联邦法官阻止了反恐和选举资助工作。 《SAVE 法案》要求选民在投票时提供公民身份证明，但该法案在参议院陷入僵局。
但特朗普继续推动，周五告诉记者，他亲自为阿拉斯加诉讼开了绿灯：“我是那个说‘做吧’的人。”
这一策略是特朗普再次加大力度对选举管理方式施加更大控制的另一个迹象——官员们正在为接下来可能发生的事情做好准备。
“我认为有人试图奠定基础，‘如果我们赢得了这些诉讼，我们就会赢得选举’，”共和党人、前佐治亚州选举高级官员加布里埃尔·斯特林(Gabriel Sterling)在谈到阿拉斯加诉讼时表示，他曾因特朗普在2020年谎称该州存在欺诈行为而与特朗普发生过争执。 “因此，对他们来说，从战术上讲，申请和失败可能是相同的区别。”
自 2016 年初选以来，特朗普一直声称选举权被窃取，他为推翻 2020 年选举失利而进行的广泛法律和政治尝试引发了 2021 年 1 月美国国会大厦的骚乱，尽管他的党内一些人希望他继续前进。
亚利桑那州马里科帕县前共和党首席选举官员斯蒂芬·里彻 (Stephen Richer) 表示：“联邦政府是他的公司，他可以对公司做所有决定，以前从未这样做过。”
《政治》杂志联系了美国每一位共和党全州选举官员的办公室，寻求对司法部在阿拉斯加州的行动的回应。其中四家拒绝置评，其余则没有回应。他们的沉默表明特朗普在党内的影响力有多大，以及在 11 月中期选举前几天愿意反对他的人有多么少。
里彻说：“如果你是共和党人，在这个问题上反对唐纳德·特朗普的人在政治上的生存率并不高。”里彻为该县 2020 年的选举结果辩护，反对特朗普及其盟友长达数年的竞选活动，试图证明他们被操纵，之后在 2024 年的初选中被更为保守的共和党人赶下台。
亚利桑那州民主党国务卿阿德里安·丰特斯强烈反对司法部的诉讼，指责该部门“充当总统的律师”。
丰特斯在周五下午接受采访时表示：“司法部的行为方式极其政治化，这完全是不恰当的，他们因为把拇指放在天平上而失去了很多可信度。” “阿拉斯加的这次尝试，如果涉及到亚利桑那州，也会失败。”
司法部在社交媒体上发布的一份声明中表示，“有关司法部试图阻止阿拉斯加选举的说法是错误的。”相反，司法部辩称，它“寻求保护选举的完整性，符合《国家选民登记法》（由国会颁布），并确保阿拉斯加选民的意愿得到尊重。”
华盛顿州司法部长、民主党人尼克·布朗将阿拉斯加的法律申请描述为“控制选举并试图以对唐纳德·特朗普和共和党有利的方式决定结果的共同努力的一部分”。
布朗表示，他担心政府会对中期选举的结果提出异议。
“这不是假设，”布朗说。 “这就是总统多年来所做的事情，他拥有政府的全部权力，最重要的是，司法部在选举方面按照他的要求行事。”
斯特林预测，这一努力将对共和党产生适得其反的效果。
“通过谈论选举被盗，通过谈论作弊，他们正在压制自己的选票，并鼓励对手的选票，”他说。 “所以从战术上讲，我认为这在政治上是愚蠢的。”

Two former FBI agents charged over Hunter Biden probes Republicans have long accused the FBI of mishandling the laptop and the investigations into the younger Biden.
Ex-FBI employees charged with lying to Congress over Hunter Biden inquiries
Updated October 23, 2026 2:50 PM ET Originally published October 23, 2026 11:51 AM ET
Hunter Biden, son of former President Joe Biden, seen in July 2024 in Washington, DC. Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images hide caption

The Justice Department has charged two former FBI employees with making false statements to Congress in connection with the bureau's investigations into Hunter Biden and his laptop ahead of the 2020 presidential election.

Bradley Benavides and Nikki Floris each face a single criminal count stemming from testimony before lawmakers in 2023. The pair, who held senior positions on the FBI's now defunct Foreign Influence Task Force, both turned themselves in and made their initial court appearance Friday morning in Washington, D.C.

The new prosecution is the latest politically fraught case to be brought by the Justice Department since President Trump returned to the White House. It dredges back up the bizarre saga surrounding former President Joe Biden's son, Hunter Biden, and his various legal troubles that featured throughout the 2020 presidential campaign.

Hunter Biden's laptop was the subject of intense scrutiny after The New York Post reported weeks before the 2020 presidential election that the device was abandoned at a Delaware repair shop in 2019, and then obtained by President Trump's former personal lawyer Rudy Giuliani.

Republicans have long accused the FBI of mishandling the laptop and the investigations into the younger Biden. Hunter Biden was convicted of federal gun charges and later pleaded guilty to separate tax offenses. (Joe Biden signed a full and unconditional pardon for his son in December 2024.)

In a statement on X , the U.S. attorney for Washington, D.C., Jeanine Pirro, said Floris and Benavides "allegedly lied to Congress about their roles in the FBI's Hunter Biden investigations, with one claiming they only learned about it from Wikipedia — despite evidence showing their involvement in helping shape the public narrative about Hunter Biden's laptop right before the election."

Prosecutors charged Benavides and Floris by criminal complaint, which means prosecutors have yet to secure an indictment from a grand jury. Under the second Trump administration, grand juries in the nation's capital and other cities have refused on several occasions to return indictments in high-profile, politically charged cases.

At a court hearing Friday morning, Magistrate Judge Zia Faruqui noted that both of the defendants have "sparkling backgrounds" in federal law enforcement and were longtime dedicated public servants. He also noted that charging them by criminal complaint for conduct that is "quite old" is unusual.
Benavides, 56, and Floris, 46, are due back in court for a preliminary hearing on Tuesday.
In a statement, Floris' attorneys called her a "patriot" who served as "dedicated FBI intelligence officer for nearly 20 years."

"Yet today, the DOJ has accused her falsely of a crime on the say-so of politicians, not on the facts. It's no coincidence the government is filing these nonsense charges now, years later, on the eve of an election," they added.
Agents search Rep. Omar's D.C. home; DOJ says it's part of criminal investigation

The Post reported Hunter Biden's laptop showed wrongdoing by then-Democratic nominee Joe Biden, who subsequently won the election. Some of the data on the laptop was later ascertained to belong to Hunter Biden. House Republicans subsequently launched an impeachment inquiry into President Biden, focusing on Hunter Biden's business dealings at the time his father was vice president. But no evidence has ever been presented that Joe Biden financially gained from his son's business activities.
The complaint alleges that Benavides and Floris both had real-time knowledge of the Hunter Biden investigations, including into his laptop, in their top posts on the Foreign Influence Task Force.

前联邦调查局雇员被控在亨特·拜登调查中向国会撒谎
更新于 2026 年 10 月 23 日下午 2:50（美国东部时间） 最初发布于 2026 年 10 月 23 日上午 11:51（美国东部时间）
前总统乔·拜登的儿子亨特·拜登于 2024 年 7 月出现在华盛顿特区。安娜摇钱树/盖蒂图片社隐藏标题栏
司法部指控两名前联邦调查局雇员在 2020 年总统大选前调查亨特·拜登及其笔记本电脑时向国会做出虚假陈述。
布拉德利·贝纳维德斯 (Bradley Benavides) 和尼基·弗洛里斯 (Nikki Floris) 均因 2023 年在立法者面前作证而面临一项刑事指控。两人曾在联邦调查局 (FBI) 现已解散的外国影响特别工作组中担任高级职务，两人均于周五上午在华盛顿特区自首并首次出庭。
新的起诉是特朗普总统重返白宫以来司法部提起的最新一起充满政治争议的案件。它挖掘了围绕前总统乔·拜登之子亨特·拜登的离奇传奇，以及他在 2020 年总统竞选期间遇到的各种法律麻烦。
在 2020 年总统大选前几周，《纽约邮报》报道称，亨特·拜登的笔记本电脑于 2019 年被遗弃在特拉华州的一家维修店，随后被特朗普总统的前私人律师鲁迪·朱利安尼获得，此后，亨特·拜登的笔记本电脑成为了严格审查的对象。
共和党人长期以来一直指责联邦调查局对笔记本电脑和对年轻拜登的调查处理不当。亨特·拜登被判犯有联邦枪支罪，后来承认了单独的税务犯罪。 （乔·拜登于 2024 年 12 月签署了对其儿子的全面无条件赦免。）
华盛顿特区联邦检察官珍妮·皮罗 (Jeanine Pirro) 在 X 网站上发表的一份声明中表示，弗洛里斯和贝纳维德斯“据称就他们在联邦调查局亨特·拜登调查中的角色向国会撒谎，其中一人声称他们只是从维基百科了解到此事，尽管有证据表明他们参与了在大选前帮助塑造有关亨特·拜登笔记本电脑的公众叙述。”
检察官对贝纳维德斯和弗洛里斯提起刑事诉讼，这意味着检察官尚未获得大陪审团的起诉。在特朗普第二届政府执政期间，美国首都和其他城市的大陪审团多次拒绝对备受瞩目的政治指控案件发出起诉书。
在周五上午的法庭听证会上，治安法官齐亚·法鲁基指出，两名被告在联邦执法部门都有“耀眼的背景”，并且是长期敬业的公务员。他还指出，通过刑事诉讼指控他们的行为“相当古老”，这是不寻常的。
56 岁的贝纳维德斯和 46 岁的弗洛里斯将于周二返回法庭参加初步听证会。
弗洛里斯的律师在一份声明中称她为“爱国者”，“担任联邦调查局情报官员近 20 年”。
“然而今天，司法部根据政客的说法，而不是根据事实，错误地指控她犯罪。几年后，在选举前夕，政府提出这些无稽之谈的指控并非巧合，”他们补充道。
特工搜查众议员奥马尔在华盛顿的家；美国司法部表示这是刑事调查的一部分
据《华盛顿邮报》报道，亨特·拜登的笔记本电脑显示当时的民主党候选人乔·拜登有不当行为，后者随后赢得了选举。后来确定笔记本电脑上的一些数据属于亨特·拜登。众议院共和党人随后对拜登总统发起弹劾调查，重点关注亨特·拜登在其父亲担任副总统期间的商业交易。但没有证据表明乔·拜登从儿子的商业活动中获得了经济利益。
起诉书称，贝纳维德斯和弗洛里斯都在外国影响力特别工作组的高层帖子中实时了解了亨特·拜登的调查情况，包括他的笔记本电脑。

summary: Republican senator faces critical re-election battle in state where president’s trade war has outraged voters Donald Trump dropped some of the US’s tariffs on Canada on Friday to “better serve the public interest” the White House said, handing a win to Susan C
summary_zh: 共和党参议员在该州面临关键的连任之战，总统的贸易战激怒了选民唐纳德·特朗普放弃了美国的一些政策
body_en: Trump drops some Canada tariffs in bid to boost embattled Susan Collins in Maine | US politics | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation
Trump drops some Canada tariffs in bid to boost embattled Susan Collins in Maine
Republican senator faces critical re-election battle in state where president’s trade war has outraged voters

Donald Trump dropped some of the US’s tariffs on Canada on Friday to “better serve the public interest” the White House said, handing a win to Susan Collins, the embattled Republican senator for Maine, as she faces a tight re-election campaign that will help determine whether Democrats can flip control of Congress.

Collins announced that the exemptions would apply to nine agricultural products, including blueberries, potatoes, apples and seaweed. She added that many of the state’s farmers rely on specialized equipment and materials from across the border that are “unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense”.

“In my repeated conversations with Ambassador Greer, Secretary Lutnick, and other senior administration officials, I have asked for tariff relief for these important products, and I will continue working directly with administration officials to seek additional relief and encourage a broader trade agreement with Canada, our neighbor, ally, and largest trading partner,” she wrote.

The White House also specified that certain processing equipment – such as plywood sheets, packing boxes, paper products, and certain machinery – would be removed from its tariffs. These materials can be crucial for Maine businesses operating close to the border.

“President Trump is further refining the scope of the July 20 and September 8 actions to better serve the public interest, and to ensure these measures continue to effectively offset the burden or disadvantage to US commerce from Canada’s discriminatory measures,” the White House said in a news release.

Collins, who has served in the Senate for nearly 30 years, is running for re-election against Troy Jackson, a Democrat who has served in the Maine state senate and is a former logger. The race is crucial for the Democratic party’s hopes of flipping control of the chamber, and is so far considered a toss-up.
‘It’s just getting worse’: anger in Maine over Trump’s trade war with close neighbor Canada

The trade war between Canada and Maine has touched a nerve in the state, which relies heavily on commerce with Canada. Many of the industries most entrenched in the state’s history – such as logging, lobstering and fishing – were expected to take a hit after Trump’s tariff announcements this year.

Earlier this week, the Canadian prime minister, Mark Carney, said American tariffs hurt both American and Canadian households. He added that auto exports to the US had so far fallen 10%, and US exports to Canada have fallen by more than 20%.

“US tariffs have upended a trade bargain that’s existed for decades,” Carney said. “They’ve raised costs for American families while putting Ontario workers and businesses at a disadvantage and under a cloud of uncertainty.”

After Trump placed a 50% tariff on certain Canadian goods, which began on 22 August, Canada announced its own retaliatory tariffs in response, ranging from 15% to 50% on $20bn worth of American goods. Canada later withdrew its tariffs on American seafood, which helped Maine’s fisheries in particular.

Maine is considered a purple state, and many within the state – including Collins – consider themselves to have an independent streak. Collins has frequently sought to distance herself from Trump, particularly when it comes to his trade policies, and has broken with her party more than any other Republican senator since Trump took office, according to a New York Times analysis of her voting record.
But her efforts to vote against Trump’s policies have rarely succeeded in his second term so far, the analysis found.

Jackson has frequently seized on this line of attack since replacing Graham Platner on the Democratic ticket. At a television debate earlier this month, Jackson also pointed to Collins’s crucial vote to confirm the conservative supreme court justice Brett Kavanaugh. The court subsequently overturned Roe v Wade.
“Tonight is about who you stand with when it matters,” Jackson said in his opening statement.
Democrats argued the decision to drop some Canadian tariffs was an admission by the White House that Trump’s policies were unpopular.
Ron Wyden, the top Democrat on the Senate finance committee, called the move a “desperate, 11th hour attempt to save Susan Collins’ political career”.

特朗普取消了加拿大的部分关税，以提振缅因州陷入困境的苏珊·柯林斯(Susan Collins)
共和党参议员在总统的贸易战激怒选民的州面临关键的连任之战
白宫表示，唐纳德·特朗普周五取消了美国对加拿大的部分关税，以“更好地服务公共利益​​”，这让陷入困境的缅因州共和党参议员苏珊·柯林斯(Susan Collins)获胜，她面临一场激烈的连任竞选，这将有助于决定民主党能否扭转国会的控制权。
柯林斯宣布豁免将适用于九种农产品，包括蓝莓、土豆、苹果和海藻。她补充说，该州的许多农民依赖来自跨境的专业设备和材料，这些设备和材料“无法从美国供应商那里获得，或者在不产生大量费用的情况下无法更换”。
她写道：“在我与格里尔大使、卢特尼克国务卿和其他高级政府官员的反复交谈中，我已要求减免这些重要产品的关税，我将继续与政府官员直接合作，寻求更多减免，并鼓励与我们的邻国、盟友和最大贸易伙伴加拿大达成更广泛的贸易协定。”
白宫还明确规定，某些加工设备——如胶合板、包装盒、纸制品和某些机械——将被免除关税。这些材料对于缅因州边境附近的企业至关重要。
白宫在一份新闻稿中表示：“特朗普总统正在进一步细化7月20日和9月8日行动的范围，以更好地服务于公共利益，并确保这些措施继续有效抵消加拿大歧视性措施给美国商业带来的负担或不利。”
已在参议院任职近 30 年的柯林斯正在竞选连任，对手是曾在缅因州参议院任职、前伐木工的民主党人特洛伊·杰克逊 (Troy Jackson)。这场竞选对于民主党夺取众议院控制权的希望至关重要，但迄今为止仍被认为是一场难以抉择的比赛。
“情况越来越糟”：缅因州对特朗普与近邻加拿大的贸易战感到愤怒
加拿大和缅因州之间的贸易战触动了该州的神经，该州严重依赖与加拿大的贸易。在特朗普今年宣布关税后，该州历史上最根深蒂固的许多行业——例如伐木、龙虾和渔业——预计将受到打击。
本周早些时候，加拿大总理马克·卡尼表示，美国的关税损害了美国和加拿大的家庭。他补充说，迄今为止，美国对美国的汽车出口下降了10%，美国对加拿大的出口下降了20%以上。
卡尼表示：“美国的关税颠覆了存在了数十年的贸易协议。” “他们提高了美国家庭的成本，同时使安大略省的工人和企业处于不利地位并处于不确定性的阴云之下。”
在特朗普于 8 月 22 日开始对某些加拿大商品征收 50% 关税后，加拿大也宣布了报复性关税作为回应，对价值 200 亿美元的美国商品征收 15% 至 50% 不等的关税。加拿大后来取消了对美国海鲜的关税，这对缅因州的渔业尤其有利。
缅因州被认为是一个紫色州，该州的许多人——包括柯林斯——认为自己有独立倾向。 《纽约时报》对柯林斯投票记录的分析显示，柯林斯经常试图与特朗普保持距离，特别是在涉及特朗普的贸易政策时，自特朗普上任以来，她与共和党的决裂比任何其他共和党参议员都多。
但分析发现，到目前为止，她投票反对特朗普政策的努力在特朗普第二任期内很少取得成功。
自从取代格雷厄姆·普拉特纳成为民主党候选人以来，杰克逊经常利用这一路线进行攻击。在本月早些时候的一场电视辩论中，杰克逊还指出了柯林斯对确认保守派最高法院法官布雷特·卡瓦诺的关键投票。法院随后推翻了罗伊诉韦德案。
杰克逊在开场白中说：“今晚的关键是在重要的时候你与谁站在一起。”
民主党人认为，取消部分加拿大关税的决定是白宫承认特朗普的政策不受欢迎。
参议院财政委员会民主党领袖罗恩·怀登 (Ron Wyden) 称此举是“为挽救苏珊·柯林斯 (Susan Collins) 的政治生涯而进行的最后 11 小时的绝望尝试”。

body_en: New Trump rule allows hunters to bait bears in Alaska with doughnuts, bacon and more | Trump administration | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation
New Trump rule allows hunters to bait bears in Alaska with doughnuts, bacon and more
Critics decry Trump administration rule that lets hunters lure bears with human foods on federal lands in Alaska

A new Trump administration rule allows hunters to bait bears on federal lands in Alaska with bacon, doughnuts, meat scraps or other human foods typically used to help kill the trophy animals at close range.

Opponents say the practice will cause bears to be more aggressive around humans, and allege that the rule change is a political gift to largely rightwing trophy hunters. The rule replaces a 2024 Biden administration rule that banned the practice, and environmental groups criticized the move as “indefensible and inexcusable”.

“We are discouraged to see this rule come back, specifically the bear baiting piece which is cruel and dangerous, not only to wildlife but the public as well,” said Drew Robertson, senior regulatory specialist for Humane World for Animals .

The US interior department on Friday published the rule on the federal register, and it will take effect in mid-November. It marks the latest in a series of rule changes at the state and federal levels since 2023 that allow trophy hunters to use what critics say are barbaric and unethical practices to kill animals.

Doug Burgum, the secretary of the interior, wrote in a press release that the latest rule was developed in response to demands by Alaska residents and it was a “commonsense framework and gives Alaskans a stronger voice in decisions affecting the lands, wildlife and traditions they know best”.

The federal rule does not list specific foods that are allowed, but it defers to state rules, which allow for baiting, and hunters typically use “the cheapest and most effective food, which is high fat and high sugar”, said Nicholas Arrivo, a managing attorney at Animal Protection Law. Hunters typically put food in a steel drum or garbage can, monitor the bait, then set up from a nearby blind from which they kill the bear at short range, Arrivo said.
The practice raises broader ethical questions around the spirit and intent of sport hunting.
“It is a more extreme practice than the hunting traditions that people think of, and many hunters would not see this as a fair chase,” Robertson said.

The move comes after Alaska and federal officials in recent years started allowing sport hunters to hunt big game with controversial practices, like shooting bears from helicopters, shooting swimming caribou from motor boats, killing wolf pups in their dens and using artificial lights to draw bears out of the dens to kill them. The bear baiting is not highly unusual as about a dozen states allow similar practices, but more do not.
The rule change came at the direction of Donald Trump in an executive order , called Unleashing Alaska’s Extraordinary Resource Potential, which was issued in his second administration’s early days.

“It was a priority for the president … and he included direction to reissue this rule, which says that there is a political motivation, not something that seems to be derived from careful consideration,” Robertson said.

This baiting rule has a long history. A ban was first put in place by Barack Obama’s administration, then undone by the first Trump administration. Litigation upheld the Obama rule and overturned the Trump rule. The Biden administration then reimplemented the rule in 2024, largely because science shows that the practice will make bears more aggressive, and put park visitors’ lives at risk.

Though the Trump administration has said the rule was designed to give the state more control over the land, the lands are federal and Congress created the federal land program to give the federal government decision-making power, not state governments, Arrivo said. He said it “is anathema to federal land management goals … of preserving wildlife diversity”.

Though no decision has yet been made about a lawsuit, Arrivo said the interior department’s decision to fully scrap the 2024 rule that underwent a more robust scientific process “doesn’t smell right and raises questions about the legality of this rule”.
body_zh: 特朗普新规定允许猎人在阿拉斯加用甜甜圈、培根等引诱熊特朗普政府 |卫报 跳到主要内容 跳到导航
特朗普新规定允许猎人在阿拉斯加用甜甜圈、培根等引诱熊
批评者谴责特朗普政府允许猎人在阿拉斯加联邦土地上用人类食物引诱熊的规定
特朗普政府的一项新规定允许猎人在阿拉斯加的联邦土地上用培根、甜甜圈、肉渣或其他通常用于近距离杀死战利品动物的人类食物来引诱熊。
反对者表示，这种做法将导致熊对人类更具攻击性，并声称规则的改变对大多数右翼战利品猎人来说是一份政治礼物。该规则取代了 2024 年拜登政府禁止这种做法的规则，环保组织批评此举“站不住脚、不可原谅”。
人道动物世界高级监管专家德鲁·罗伯逊 (Drew Robertson) 表示：“看到这条规则重新出现，我们感到很沮丧，特别是捕熊的行为，不仅对野生动物而且对公众来说都是残酷和危险的。”
美国内政部周五在联邦公报上公布了这一规定，并将于 11 月中旬生效。这是自 2023 年以来州和联邦层面一系列规则变化中的最新一项，这些规则允许战利品猎人使用批评者所说的野蛮和不道德的做法来杀死动物。
内政部长道格·布尔古姆在一份新闻稿中写道，最新规则是根据阿拉斯加居民的要求制定的，它是一个“常识性框架，让阿拉斯加人在影响他们最了解的土地、野生动物和传统的决策中拥有更强的发言权”。
动物保护法的管理律师尼古拉斯·阿里沃（Nicholas Arrivo）表示，联邦规定没有列出允许的具体食物，但它遵循州规定，允许使用诱饵，猎人通常使用“最便宜、最有效的食物，即高脂肪和高糖”。阿里沃说，猎人通常将食物放入钢桶或垃圾桶中，监控诱饵，然后在附近的百叶窗上设置诱饵，在近距离杀死熊。
这种做法引发了围绕运动狩猎的精神和意图的更广泛的道德问题。
“这是一种比人们想象的狩猎传统更为极端的做法，许多猎人不会认为这是一次公平的追逐，”罗伯逊说。
在此之前，阿拉斯加和联邦官员近年来开始允许运动狩猎者使用有争议的做法来狩猎大型动物，例如从直升机上射杀熊，从摩托艇上射杀游泳的驯鹿，在狼穴中杀死狼崽，以及使用人造光将熊从狼穴中吸引出来杀死它们。诱熊事件并不罕见，大约有十几个州允许类似的做法，但更多州则不允许。
这一规则的改变是在唐纳德·特朗普的一项行政命令的指导下进行的，该命令名为“释放阿拉斯加的非凡资源潜力”，该命令是在他的第二届政府初期发布的。
罗伯逊说：“这是总统的首要任务……他包括重新发布这条规则的指示，该规则表明存在政治动机，而不是经过仔细考虑而得出的东西。”
这种诱饵规则有着悠久的历史。巴拉克·奥巴马政府首先实施了一项禁令，然后被特朗普第一届政府撤销。诉讼维持了奥巴马的规则并推翻了特朗普的规则。拜登政府随后在 2024 年重新实施了这一规定，主要是因为科学表明，这种做法会让熊变得更具攻击性，并使公园游客的生命面临危险。
阿里沃说，尽管特朗普政府表示，该规则的目的是让州对土地有更多的控制权，但土地是联邦的，国会制定联邦土地计划是为了赋予联邦政府决策权，而不是州政府。他表示，这“违背了保护野生动物多样性的联邦土地管理目标……”。
尽管尚未就诉讼做出决定，但阿里沃表示，内政部决定完全废除经过更严格的科学程序的 2024 年规则，“听起来不太对劲，并引发了人们对该规则合法性的质疑”。

summary_zh: 即使拥有数百万美元的战争资金，这位美国代表仍面临着与民主党人丽贝卡·贝内特争夺席位的激烈斗争
body_en: Tom Kean had everything going for him. Then the Republican New Jersey congressman disappeared | New Jersey | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation
Tom Kean had everything going for him. Then the Republican New Jersey congressman disappeared
Even with a multimillion-dollar war chest, the US representative faces a stiff fight for his seat from Democrat Rebecca Bennett
The stars above New Jersey seemed aligned for Tom Kean Jr.

The Republican congressman had a war chest of more than $2.4m in February, an endorsement from Donald Trump and a district whose lines were redrawn in 2022 to benefit his party. He was an established political figure with widespread name recognition, thanks to his father’s stint as a well-regarded governor of New Jersey .

Kean, 58, was not seen in Congress, or public, for more than three months and missed 100 votes without explanation – as Trump’s war on Iran piled pressure on the US economy, and the president threatened fresh tariffs on global imports.

Democrats meanwhile selected a moderate, Rebecca Bennett, to challenge Kean for his seat. Kean, who resurfaced at the end of June, is now in the midst of a tight race in one of the wealthiest districts in the nation.
In an ominous sign for Republicans, the closely watched Cook Political Report moved New Jersey’s seventh congressional district from “toss-up” to “lean Democrat” last month.

Most Republicans fighting for re-election while aligned with Trump are grappling with the impact of the president’s growing unpopularity . His war with Iran has driven the cost of fuel and groceries up, angering the voters who were promised lower prices under his administration.

But Kean has also endured months of discourse – and national headlines – over his prolonged absence, and reserved public appearances. When he returned at the end of June, the congressman said he had been hospitalized for depression.
“I think mental health issues aside, which are serious ... I don’t think he handled the issue very well,” said Albie, a New Jersey voter attending a No Kings protest in New Providence last weekend.

Mike Johnson, the Republican speaker of the House of Representatives, appeared to agree in August. “You know, if it were me, I would have done it a little sooner,” he told the New York Times of Kean’s reluctance to explain his absence.
Johnson, like many, is sympathetic to Kean’s health condition, which affects millions of Americans.

Since his return, Kean has been accused of avoiding the media spotlight. His campaign denied a New York Times reporter entry to an event attended by other media outlets in August; he refused to take questions from reporters after participating in a livestreamed debate against Bennett, his Democratic opponent.
The Guardian sent two emails to Kean’s campaign requesting an interview, or the opportunity to attend a campaign event. They went unanswered.

Harrison Neely, Kean’s campaign manager, did not respond to an initial text message containing the same requests earlier this week. He did, however, respond to a second message asking for a brief interview on Thursday.

“I think the narrative that congressman Kean doesn’t engage with the press is simply false,” said Neely, adding that the campaign prefers to communicate with voters directly. (On Thursday, New York Magazine published an article saying its multiple requests for an interview went ignored.)

Kean does give interviews, mostly to local reporters , and the campaign has invited local outlets to cover events . Neely said the campaign most recently challenged Bennett to a debate on WRNJ, a local radio station. However, the Bennett campaign declined to participate.
“So you know, I think it’s basically fair to say that congressman Kean does more local press engagements than any sitting member of the New Jersey delegation,” Neely said.
Bennett, a political newcomer, is cautiously optimistic that she can flip a battleground district in New Jersey for the Democrats in next month’s midterm.

尽管拥有数百万美元的战争资金，这位美国代表仍面临着与民主党丽贝卡·贝内特争夺席位的激烈斗争
新泽西州上空的星星似乎与小汤姆·基恩对齐。
这位共和党国会议员在 2 月份拥有超过 240 万美元的战争资金，这是唐纳德·特朗普和一个选区的支持，该选区的界线在 2022 年被重新划定，以使他的政党受益。由于他父亲曾担任备受推崇的新泽西州州长，他是一位享有广泛知名度的政治人物。
58 岁的基恩已经超过三个多月没有出现在国会或公众场合，并且在没有任何解释的情况下错过了 100 次投票——特朗普对伊朗的战争给美国经济带来了压力，而且总统威胁对全球进口产品征收新的关税。
与此同时，民主党选择了温和派丽贝卡·贝内特来挑战基恩的席位。基恩于六月底重新露面，目前正在全国最富有的地区之一进行激烈的竞选。
对共和党人来说，这是一个不祥的迹象，备受关注的库克政治报告上个月将新泽西州第七国会选区从“摇摆不定”转变为“倾向民主党”。
大多数在与特朗普结盟的同时争取连任的共和党人都在努力应对总统日益不受欢迎的影响。他与伊朗的战争推高了燃料和食品杂货的成本，激怒了在他的政府下承诺降低价格的选民。
但基恩也因长期缺席和保留公开露面而遭受了数月的讨论和全国头条新闻。当他六月底回来时，这位国会议员说他因抑郁症住院了。
“我认为，抛开心理健康问题不谈，这是很严重的……我认为他处理这个问题的方式不是很好，”上周末参加新普罗维登斯反对国王抗议活动的新泽西州选民阿尔比说。
众议院共和党议长迈克·约翰逊 (Mike Johnson) 8 月份似乎也同意这一观点。 “你知道，如果是我，我会早一点这么做，”他告诉《纽约时报》，基恩不愿解释他的缺席原因。
和许多人一样，约翰逊对基恩的健康状况表示同情，基恩的健康状况影响着数百万美国人。
自从回归后，基恩就被指责回避媒体的关注。他的竞选团队拒绝《纽约时报》记者进入八月份其他媒体参加的活动；在参加与民主党对手贝内特的直播辩论后，他拒绝接受记者提问。
《卫报》向基恩的竞选团队发送了两封电子邮件，要求接受采访或参加竞选活动的机会。他们没有得到答复。
基恩的竞选经理哈里森·尼利没有回复本周早些时候包含相同请求的最初短信。不过，他确实在周四回复了第二条要求进行简短采访的消息。
尼利说：“我认为国会议员基恩不与媒体接触的说法完全是错误的。”他补充说，竞选团队更喜欢直接与选民沟通。 （周四，《纽约杂志》发表文章称，其多次采访请求均被忽视。）
基恩确实接受采访，主要是接受当地记者的采访，竞选活动也邀请了当地媒体报道活动。尼利表示，竞选活动最近向贝内特提出挑战，要求他在当地广播电台 WRNJ 上进行辩论。然而，贝内特竞选团队拒绝参加。
“所以你知道，我认为可以公平地说，国会议员基恩比新泽西州代表团的任何现任成员都进行了更多的当地新闻活动，”尼利说。
贝内特是一位政治新人，她对自己能够在下个月的中期选举中将新泽西州的一个战场选区转变为民主党持谨慎乐观的态度。

title_en: Vance front and center in Republican midterms push – is this a dry run for a White House bid?
title_zh: 万斯在共和党中期选举的推动中处于领先地位——这是一次入主白宫的预演吗？

body_en: Vance front and center in Republican midterms push – is this a dry run for a White House bid? | JD Vance | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation
Vance front and center in Republican midterms push – is this a dry run for a White House bid?
Vice-president’s visibility has risen as Trump’s popularity wanes, but path to inherit Maga throne is more complicated than it may seem
A day after JD Vance suggested Donald Trump would endorse him if he runs for president, the vice-president shifted awkwardly in the Oval Office as his boss was asked about the remark.

“He’s a very talented person, and he’s a very good person,” Trump said of the man standing behind him, with a forced smile this week. “But we’ve literally – I don’t think we’ve ever talked about,” the president claimed, leaving the assertion unconfirmed.

As the campaign for the congressional midterms has intensified, the vice-president’s visibility has risen. If Trump and Vance truly have yet to discuss his presidential prospects, they are firmly in the minority in Washington.

While many aspects of this political era remain extraordinary, the core question hanging over Vance is one that has been asked for decades: is the vice-presidency a platform, or a poisoned chalice, for those who dare to dream of higher office?

Having spent only two years as a US senator before Trump tapped him in 2024 as his running mate, Vance has hit the campaign trail in recent weeks like a seasoned veteran – making stump speeches on behalf of Republican candidates as the party struggles to retain its grip on the US Senate and House of Representatives amid Trump’s plunging approval ratings.

He has held rallies in states such as Iowa, Florida, Texas, Alaska, Georgia, Michigan and his native Ohio in a criss-crossing odyssey that compares to that of Trump, who has told voters to behave as though he were on the ballot.

With secretary of state Marco Rubio – widely seen as his main rival for the next Republican nomination – focused on fighting the fires sparked by Trump’s global agenda, analysts believe Vance’s campaigning roadshow is intended as a dry run for a 2028 presidential bid. Each stop enables him to build contacts and goodwill, which he can call on in the likely event of him seeking the nomination in less than two years’ time.

Matthew Dallek, a political historian at George Washington University, said Vance was trying to “build up chits” aimed at making Trump’s Make America Great Again (Maga) movement “remember that he was a good soldier”.

“He is trying to do what a lot of smart vice-presidents have done throughout history, and that’s to earn some credit out there with state and and congressional candidates,” said Rick Wilson, a former Republican strategist who now runs the anti-Trump Lincoln Project , “so that when he kicks up a campaign machine in two years, people owe him something”.

Time and again over the past two years Vance has slipped into “explainer-in-chief” mode, providing a more palatable narrative in the wake of Trump’s more extreme statements, impulses or policy decisions. Critics have branded the practice as “sane-washing”, whereby the verbally dextrous vice-president tries to use his facile language skills to normalize otherwise outlandish utterances or actions.

In recent months, Vance – after publishing a book on his conversion to Catholicism – has rationalized a meme posted by Trump on his Truth Social platform that seemed to depict him as Jesus Christ. He also tried to deny , or at least reinterpret, Trump’s words when he told journalists that he did not think about Americans’ financial situation in conducting the war with Iran.

And just last weekend, he defended the president against charges of corruption in a CBS town hall event, when told that many voters were concerned that Trump was making money from cryptocurrency . “You can make all kinds of criticisms of our policies and decisions, but I’ve not once seen evidence that Donald Trump has enriched himself,” Vance replied. (Trump’s personal fortune has surged from $2.3bn in 2024 to $6.5bn this year, according to Forbes.)

His slavishly supportive comments have naturally been welcomed by Trump, but they also highlight the problems Vance may face in trying to become the president’s heir as head of the Maga movement. While unstinting loyalty is the coin of the realm in the Trump-dominated Republicans , the president’s vice-like grip on the party presents a fundamental challenge to anyone hoping to step out from his shadow and assert an independent persona aimed at wooing the base.

The fate of Trump’s first vice-president, Mike Pence – who had to be evacuated to an underground shelter in the US Capitol on 6 January 2021, as pro-Trump rioters called for his execution following his refusal to overturn the 2020 presidential election result – serves as a salutary warning of the high price that autonomy may exact.

“Vance has two choices,” argued Kurt Bardella , a former Republican congressional staffer who left the party in 2017. “Either ride Trump all the way to the island of irrelevancy, or break with him and incur his wrath.”

“Neither are great options,” he added. “The political reality is that anyone who is tethered to Trump will face an electoral backlash. Trump will continue to erode democratic norms as his grip on power wanes.

“That will force people like Vance into untenable positions that they have proven unable to navigate. They’ll have to either double down on the crazy or break up with him and alienate the primary base he needs to win the nomination.”

万斯在共和党中期选举的推动中处于领先地位——这是一次入主白宫的预演吗？
随着特朗普声望的下降，副总统的知名度有所上升，但继承马加王位的道路比看起来更复杂
就在 JD 万斯暗示唐纳德·特朗普如果竞选总统就会支持他的一天后，当他的老板被问及这一言论时，这位副总统在椭圆形办公室里尴尬地转变了态度。
“他是一个非常有才华的人，也是一个非常好的人，”特朗普本周谈到站在他身后的那个人时，脸上带着勉强的微笑。总统声称：“但我们确实——我认为我们从来没有谈论过”，但这一说法尚未得到证实。
随着国会中期选举的竞选活动愈演愈烈，副总统的知名度也随之上升。如果特朗普和万斯真的还没有讨论他的总统前景，那么他们在华盛顿绝对是少数派。
虽然这个政治时代的许多方面仍然非同寻常，但万斯面临的核心问题是几十年来一直被问到的一个问题：对于那些敢于梦想更高职位的人来说，副总统职位是一个平台，还是一个有毒的圣杯？
在特朗普于 2024 年任命他为竞选搭档之前，万斯只担任了两年的美国参议员。最近几周，万斯像一位经验丰富的老兵一样开始了竞选活动，代表共和党候选人发表巡回演讲，而在特朗普支持率大幅下滑的情况下，该党正在努力保持对美国参议院和众议院的控制权。
他在爱荷华州、佛罗里达州、得克萨斯州、阿拉斯加州、佐治亚州、密歇根州和他的家乡俄亥俄州等州举行了一次纵横交错的集会，与特朗普的集会相比，特朗普告诉选民要表现得就像他在选票上一样。
由于国务卿马可·卢比奥 — — 被广泛视为他下一届共和党提名的主要竞争对手 — — 专注于扑灭特朗普全球议程引发的大火，分析人士认为，万斯的竞选路演旨在为 2028 年总统竞选进行预演。每一次停留都使他能够建立联系和善意，如果他在不到两年的时间内寻求提名，他可以利用这些联系和善意。
乔治华盛顿大学政治历史学家马修·达莱克表示，万斯正试图“集结”，旨在让特朗普的“让美国再次伟大”(Maga)运动“记住他是一名好士兵”。
“他正试图做历史上许多聪明的副总统所做的事情，那就是赢得州和国会候选人的信任，”现任反特朗普林肯项目负责人的前共和党策略师里克·威尔逊(Rick Wilson)说，“这样当他在两年内启动竞选机器时，人们就欠他一些东西”。
过去两年里，万斯一次又一次地陷入“总解释者”模式，在特朗普发表更极端的言论、冲动或政策决定后，提供更容易接受的叙述。批评者将这种做法称为“理智清洗”，即这位善于言辞的副总统试图利用他流畅的语言技能来使原本古怪的言论或行为正常化。
近几个月来，万斯在出版了一本关于他皈依天主教的书后，对特朗普在他的真相社交平台上发布的一个表情包进行了合理化，该表情包似乎将他描绘成耶稣基督。当特朗普告诉记者他在与伊朗作战时没有考虑美国的财务状况时，他还试图否认或至少重新解释特朗普的话。
就在上周末，当他被告知许多选民担心特朗普从加密货币中赚钱时，他在哥伦比亚广播公司市政厅活动中为总统的腐败指控进行了辩护。 “你可以对我们的政策和决定提出各种各样的批评，但我从未见过唐纳德·特朗普为自己谋取利益的证据，”万斯回答道。 （据福布斯报道，特朗普的个人财富已从 2024 年的 23 亿美元飙升至今年的 65 亿美元。）
他的盲目支持言论自然受到特朗普的欢迎，但它们也凸显了万斯在试图成为总统继承人作为马加运动领导人时可能面临的问题。虽然无限的忠诚是特朗普主导的共和党的金币，但总统对共和党的恶习般的控制对任何希望走出他的阴影、维护独立形象、争取选民支持的人来说都是一个根本性的挑战。
特朗普的第一副总统迈克·彭斯 (Mike Pence) 于 2021 年 1 月 6 日被疏散到美国国会大厦的地下避难所，因为支持特朗普的骚乱者因拒绝推翻 2020 年总统选举结果而呼吁处决他。他的命运是对自治可能付出的高昂代价的有益警告。
“万斯有两个选择，”2017 年离开共和党的前共和党国会工作人员库尔特·巴尔德拉 (Kurt Bardella) 表示，“要么将特朗普一路推向无关紧要的岛屿，要么与他决裂并招致他的愤怒。”
“这两个都不是很好的选择，”他补充道。 “政治现实是，任何与特朗普挂钩的人都将面临选举的强烈反对。随着特朗普对权力的控制减弱，他将继续侵蚀民主规范。
“这将迫使像万斯这样的人陷入站不住脚的境地，事实证明他们无法驾驭。他们要么对疯狂的人加倍努力，要么与他分手，疏远他赢得提名所需的主要基础。”

title_en: Thune campaigns with Ashley Hinson as Senate GOP zeroes in on Iowa
title_zh: 图恩与阿什利·辛森 (Ashley Hinson) 一起竞选，参议院共和党瞄准爱荷华州
summary: Senate Majority Leader John Thune campaigned with GOP Rep. Ashley Hinson in Iowa on Friday in his latest effort to prop up Republican candidates on the campaign trail.
summary_zh: 参议院多数党领袖约翰·图恩周五在爱荷华州与共和党众议员阿什利·辛森一起竞选，这是他支持共和党候选人的最新努力。
body_en: Thune campaigns with Ashley Hinson as Senate Republicans view Iowa as a majority-maker - CBS News

Sioux City, Iowa — Senate Majority Leader John Thune campaigned with GOP Rep. Ashley Hinson in Iowa on Friday in his latest effort to prop up Republican candidates on the campaign trail, emphasizing how the Hawkeye State, reliably red in recent elections, now may hold the key to control of the Senate .
"The majority in the United States Senate must run through the state of Iowa," Thune said.

Iowa is one of several states that entered the midterm conversation in recent months, with a number of Senate races appearing in play for Democrats despite being unthinkable at the start of the cycle. And in the final sprint to Election Day, Republicans are doing everything they can to hold the line.

Speaking at a roundtable event at a bar and grill alongside Hinson and a half dozen local workers, Thune warned that if Democrats win the majority, the next two years will be spent doing "nothing but investigations and impeachment trials and all that sort of thing." He said, "That's not a good place for the American people to be."
"There's a lot more to do. And we look forward to rolling up our sleeves and lacing them up and getting after it," Thune said. "But we've got to get through Nov. 3."

Hinson is facing off against Democratic state Rep. Josh Turek for an open Senate seat. Democrats haven't won a U.S. Senate race in Iowa since 2008, but as affordability issues squeeze Iowans, with extra strain on farmers, polls have shown Hinson and Turek locked in a dead heat.

Hinson, a former local news anchor who's represented Iowa in the House since 2021, has emphasized the need for someone responsible at the wheel for Iowans, speaking to voters about being a minivan mom and joking that her experience parenting teenagers has prepared her to work with "unreasonable people" in Congress. And although she initially campaigned on her close proximity to the White House, she's pushed back in recent weeks over the unpopular war in Iran and high energy prices . But she still appeared alongside President Trump on Thursday at a rally just a few miles down the road .

Thune, who hails from neighboring South Dakota and did not attend the rally with the president, told reporters that he and Hinson had "a good full day" campaigning on Friday, including a visit to a local air base, where they heard about the need to complete a runway, along with the roundtable later on.
Speaking to reporters after the event, Thune called it "a great opportunity" to hear the issues on the "hearts and minds" of Iowa voters.
"And I think, like a lot of places, it's economic issues," he added.

At the event, local business leaders, including the head of a fertilizer distribution network and a restaurant owner, spoke of high prices, the availability of childcare, supply chain issues and housing and diesel costs. Hinson outlined a list of priorities, including making the no-tax-on-tips policy permanent, focusing on housing and lowering costs for farmers.
In recent weeks, Hinson has pushed for suspending the gas tax, pausing diesel exports from the United States and offering diesel relief to farmers and truckers .

Thune said as someone who represents a neighboring state, "we share a lot of common issues that we deal with — whether it's transportation or whether it's national security issues, water, a whole bunch of things that kind of bind us together."

Asked about the political environment, as the president and the Senate majority leader made visits to one of the state's reddest areas to boost her candidacy, Hinson told CBS News that she's "focused on all Iowa issues and driving down prices for everyone."
"She's going border to border," Thune chimed in.
Questioned about why the race has grown so competitive in Iowa more broadly, in a state that the president won by 13 points in 2024, Thune cited "economic and political headwinds" for GOP candidates.

The picture extends to other Midwestern states, like Nebraska and Kansas , where Republicans are locked in more-competitive-than-expected contests. With 53 Republicans in the Senate, Democrats would need to flip four seats, and defend a handful of others, to take control of the chamber. And while Democrats still acknowledge that nearly everything would need to go right for them to secure the majority, it's no longer an unthinkable scenario.
But at least in Iowa, Thune expressed confidence that Hinson will pull it off.

"You're talking about a midterm election, a non-presidential year, those are all factors that, you know, sort of weigh into what the overall environment is," Thune said. "But in spite of that, she's going to win."
body_zh: 图恩与阿什利·辛森 (Ashley Hinson) 一起竞选，参议院共和党人将爱荷华州视为多数派 - 哥伦比亚广播公司 (CBS) 新闻
爱荷华州苏城——参议院多数党领袖约翰·图恩 (John Thune) 周五在爱荷华州与共和党众议员阿什利·辛森 (Ashley Hinson) 一起进行竞选活动，这是他在竞选活动中支持共和党候选人的最新努力，强调在最近的选举中可靠的红色鹰眼州现在可能掌握控制参议院的关键。
图恩说：“美国参议院的多数席位必须由爱荷华州获得。”
爱荷华州是近几个月进入中期对话的几个州之一，尽管在周期开始时这是不可想象的，但许多参议院竞选似乎对民主党有利。在选举日的最后冲刺中，共和党人正在竭尽全力坚守阵地。
图恩与辛森和六名当地工人一起在一家酒吧和烧烤店举行的圆桌会议上发表讲话，他警告说，如果民主党赢得多数席位，未来两年将“除了调查和弹劾审判以及诸如此类的事情之外什么也不做”。他说：“这对美国人民来说不是一个好地方。”
“还有很多事情要做。我们期待着卷起袖子，系好鞋带，继续努力，”图恩说。 “但我们必须熬过 11 月 3 日。”
辛森正在与民主党州众议员乔什·图雷克争夺一个空缺的参议院席位。自2008年以来，民主党在爱荷华州的美国参议院竞选中一直没有获胜，但随着负担能力问题挤压爱荷华州，农民也面临额外压力，民意调查显示辛森和图雷克陷入了胶着状态。
辛森是一名前当地新闻主播，自 2021 年以来一直在众议院代表爱荷华州。她强调需要有人为爱荷华州负责。她向选民讲述了自己是一名小型货车妈妈的经历，并开玩笑说，她养育青少年的经历让她做好了与国会“不讲道理的人”共事的准备。尽管她最初在竞选时声称自己离白宫很近，但最近几周她因不受欢迎的伊朗战争和高能源价格而有所反击。但周四，她仍然与特朗普总统一起出现在距离路几英里的一场集会上。
来自邻国南达科他州的图恩没有与总统一起参加集会，他告诉记者，他和辛森周五的竞选活动“度过了愉快的一天”，包括参观当地的一个空军基地，在那里他们听说需要完成一条跑道，并随后举行了圆桌会议。
图恩在活动结束后对记者表示，这是听取爱荷华州选民“内心”问题的“绝佳机会”。
“我认为，就像很多地方一样，这是经济问题，”他补充道。
在活动中，包括化肥分销网络负责人和餐馆老板在内的当地商界领袖谈到了高价格、儿童保育服务、供应链问题以及住房和柴油成本。辛森列出了一系列优先事项，包括永久实行小费免税政策、重点关注住房和降低农民的成本。
最近几周，辛森一直在推动暂停征收汽油税，暂停美国的柴油出口，并向农民和卡车司机提供柴油减免。
图恩表示，作为邻国的代表，“我们有很多共同处理的问题——无论是交通问题，还是国家安全问题、水问题，以及将我们联系在一起的一大堆问题。”
当被问及政治环境时，总统和参议院多数党领袖访问了该州最红的地区之一以提高她的候选资格，辛森告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，她“专注于爱荷华州的所有问题，并为每个人压低价格”。
“她要去边境到边境，”图恩插话道。
当被问及为什么爱荷华州的竞选竞争如此激烈时，总统在 2024 年以 13 个百分点的优势获胜，图恩指出共和党候选人面临“经济和政治阻力”。
这种情况也延伸到了其他中西部州，例如内布拉斯加州和堪萨斯州，这些州的共和党人陷入了比预期更加激烈的竞争。参议院有 53 名共和党人，民主党需要翻转 4 个席位，并捍卫其他少数席位，才能控制参议院。尽管民主党人仍然承认，几乎所有事情都需要顺利进行才能获得多数席位，但这不再是一个不可想象的场景。
但至少在爱荷华州，图恩表示相信辛森会成功。
图恩说：“你谈论的是中期选举，非总统选举年，这些都是影响整体环境的因素。” “但尽管如此，她还是会赢。”

Additional 178 cases of measles reported by US health authorities amid outbreak
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported 4,588 cases across the country, more than double the tally in 2025
Federal health authorities reported an additional 178 cases of measles in the US this week, as the vaccine-preventable illness continues to sicken people across at least 43 outbreaks.

The new data reported by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) comes as experts criticize the agency for lack of transparency, and as health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr takes steps to further upend US vaccine infrastructure.

The CDC reported 4,588 cases of measles across the country in 2026 as of Friday – more than double the tally for 2025. Pennsylvania alone reported 1,338 cases on the same day. The CDC also reported large outbreaks in South Carolina and Utah, both of which are reporting more than 500 cases.
CDC denies approval for high-volume measles test, citing ‘other priorities’

In spite of rising measles numbers, official tallies represent an undercount of the disease. Measles is widely regarded as one of the most contagious diseases known to medicine. Its most common symptoms – rash, runny nose, fever and cough – may not immediately send the infected to a doctor.

Measles sends one in five unvaccinated people who become infected to the hospital, and one to three people in 1,000 die of disease-related complications. The measles vaccine is 97% effective at preventing the disease. Vaccine side effects include injection-site soreness and low-grade fever. The measles vaccine has been a focal point of anti-vaccine activism for decades.

In Pennsylvania, which has had the worst outbreak in the nation for months, state authorities have reported five measles-associated deaths and are investigating a sixth. The CDC has reported three measles deaths nationally, but has refused to say where the third death took place, obscuring whether it is counting a death in Pennsylvania or elsewhere.
Kennedy reportedly asked senior CDC officials in September to remove a measles death from the official tally after he questioned whether the disease contributed to the death, according to Reuters .

In addition to criticism of how the CDC has tallied measles deaths, Health and Human Services (HHS) this week announced changes to vaccine injury reporting systems. A proposal will allow doctors to bill for reporting suspected vaccine injuries, among other changes.

The “vaccine adverse event reporting system”, or VAERS, has been a long-time fixation of the anti-vaccine movement. The system has proved useful for researchers tracking rare vaccine safety issues. However, it has also become a source of misinformation for anti-vaccine activists, who point to VAERS to make claims, however unfounded, about safety.

All vaccines have risks – a fact acknowledged by vaccinologists . Before Kennedy’s appointment to the health department, an expert panel considered each vaccine change individually to decide whether benefits outweigh risks. Kennedy fired all 17 sitting members of that board. He replaced them with members with whom he ideologically aligned. A court blocked the members’ appointment in March.

In his time as secretary, Kennedy also misleadingly claimed children get more than 90 vaccine doses ; linked vaccines to autism in spite of extensive evidence to the contrary; directed the CDC to remove claims that vaccines do not cause autism from its website; claimed the measles, mumps and rubella vaccine contains “ aborted fetal debris ”; and stated that vitamin A and cod liver oil may help children with measles, which leading physicians described as misleading.

美国卫生当局报告麻疹疫情期间新增 178 例麻疹病例
美国疾病控制与预防中心报告全国有 4,588 例病例，是 2025 年病例数的两倍多
联邦卫生当局本周报告美国新增 178 例麻疹病例，这种疫苗可预防的疾病在至少 43 次疫情中继续使人们患病。
美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 报告新数据之际，专家批评该机构缺乏透明度，而卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪 (Robert F Kennedy Jr) 则采取措施进一步颠覆美国疫苗基础设施。
截至周五，美国疾病控制和预防中心 (CDC) 报告称，2026 年全国有 4,588 例麻疹病例，是 2025 年病例数的两倍多。仅宾夕法尼亚州当天就报告了 1,338 例麻疹病例。 CDC 还报告了南卡罗来纳州和犹他州的大规模疫情爆发，这两个州均报告了 500 多例病例。
疾病预防控制中心以“其他优先事项”为由，拒绝批准大规模麻疹检测
尽管麻疹人数不断上升，但官方统计数字仍低估了这种疾病。麻疹被广泛认为是医学上已知的最具传染性的疾病之一。它最常见的症状——皮疹、流鼻涕、发烧和咳嗽——可能不会立即将感染者送去看医生。
麻疹导致五分之一未接种疫苗的感染者被送往医院，千分之一到三人死于与疾病相关的并发症。麻疹疫苗预防该疾病的有效率为 97%。疫苗副作用包括注射部位疼痛和低烧。几十年来，麻疹疫苗一直是反疫苗运动的焦点。
在宾夕法尼亚州，几个月来该州疫情最为严重，该州当局报告了五例与麻疹相关的死亡事件，并正在调查第六例。疾病预防控制中心报告了全国三例麻疹死亡病例，但拒绝透露第三例死亡病例发生在哪里，从而模糊了它是否在统计宾夕法尼亚州或其他地方的死亡病例。
据路透社报道，肯尼迪在质疑麻疹是否导致死亡后，于 9 月份要求疾病预防控制中心高级官员将麻疹死亡人数从官方统计中删除。
除了对疾病预防控制中心统计麻疹死亡人数的批评之外，卫生与公众服务部 (HHS) 本周还宣布对疫苗伤害报告系统进行更改。除其他变化外，一项提案将允许医生对报告疑似疫苗伤害进行收费。
“疫苗不良事件报告系统”（VAERS）长期以来一直是反疫苗运动的固定内容。事实证明，该系统对于研究人员追踪罕见的疫苗安全问题很有用。然而，它也成为反疫苗活动人士错误信息的来源，他们指出 VAERS 是关于安全性的说法，尽管毫无根据。
所有疫苗都有风险——这是疫苗学家承认的事实。在肯尼迪被任命为卫生部门之前，一个专家小组单独考虑了每种疫苗的变化，以决定益处是否大于风险。肯尼迪解雇了该委员会的全部 17 名现任成员。他用与他在意识形态上一致的成员取代了他们。法院于三月份阻止了这些成员的任命。
肯尼迪在担任国务卿期间还误导性地声称儿童接种了超过 90 剂疫苗；尽管有大量相反的证据，但仍将疫苗与自闭症联系起来；指示疾病预防控制中心从其网站上删除有关疫苗不会导致自闭症的声明；声称麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹疫苗含有“流产胎儿碎片”；并指出维生素 A 和鱼肝油可能有助于治疗麻疹儿童，但主流医生认为这是一种误导。

body_en: Epstein files take back seat in midterms but experts say issue has not gone away | US politics | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation
Epstein files take back seat in midterms but experts say issue has not gone away
Other voter concerns have prevailed but return of Congress likely to see renewed focus on late sex offender’s activities

As US voters head to the polls for crucial and fraught midterm elections, some survivors’ advocates in the Jeffrey Epstein investigation have expressed concern that the scandal could recede into the background.

Political experts believe, however, the Epstein issue is not going away permanently and that many voters can balance day-to-day concerns such as affordability and AI with the scandal involving the late financier and accused sex trafficker whose social circle was widespread among America’s elite.

“My greatest concern is not that the public will forget Jeffrey Epstein, but that the politicians and institutions responsible for accountability will use the chaos of world events as an excuse to move on,” said Spencer Kuvin of Goldlaw, who has represented multiple Epstein survivors.

Kuvin added: “Wars, economic crises and political controversies may dominate the headlines, but they do not erase the suffering of the victims or the unanswered questions about how Epstein and his powerful associates were allowed to operate for decades.

“Justice should not have an expiration date, and it certainly should not be dictated by the news cycle. We cannot allow the Epstein scandal to become yesterday’s news simply because today’s headlines are more urgent.”
Epstein’s attorney and accountant accused of ‘facilitating and concealing’ his crimes in lawsuit
Kuvin called for the US government to continue releasing Epstein files – which many have said were excluded from allegedly incomplete disclosures – and for Congress to demand accountability.

“It has been disappointing to have seen attention diverted from Jeffrey Epstein in the past year,” said Jennifer Freeman of Marsh Law, who represents numerous Epstein survivors in litigation surrounding his sexual abuse of teenage girls.

Freeman, however, expressed optimism about the long-term prospects of justice for survivors, saying: “While public attention may have shifted from the Epstein case, given the electoral cycle, I am confident it will command concentration and accountability shortly again.”

Freeman noted that she was continuing to pursue a lawsuit against the US government for alleged negligence “in repeatedly, for decades, dropping the ball on investigating and prosecuting Epstein”. She is also litigating a class-action lawsuit against his estate related to his collection and production of child sex abuse images.
Political experts said that Epstein might get less attention from campaigning politicians and voters, but that it was probably a temporary dip, not a permanent drop-off.

“It really does feel like everything is on fire. I think people can care about several things at once, but what’s directly affecting their lives tends to take priority,” Brittany Martinez, a Republican strategist who works as acting director of Principles First, said. “When they’re worried about gas prices, living costs and whether their government is working for them, that can push Epstein out of the immediate conversation.

“I don’t think the questions or the demand for answers have gone away; they’re just competing for attention. So I’d expect to hear less about it for stretches, rather than see it disappear altogether.”
“There’s just something every day with Trump,” said Shawn Donahue, clinical associate professor in the University at Buffalo’s department of political science.

For Donahue, timing also plays a key role. The US Congress has been in recess and without members on the House floor, so there’s not any discussion of the Epstein Files Transparency Act’s proposed new iteration. This bill, the Epstein Files Transparency Act II , seeks to address what advocates have said are shortfalls in the present EFTA – such as an absence of enforcement mechanisms.

“It kind of feels like whenever Congress comes back into session, this probably starts to become more of an issue again, and especially if Democrats are looking at being in control of one or maybe both chambers of Congress,” Donahue said.
Should Democrats win the house, as polls project, Donahue expects they will swiftly “put Republicans on the spot” with Epstein. “Democrats are ready to start on the investigation from day one.”

爱泼斯坦文件在中期选举中退居二线，但专家表示问题并未消失
其他选民的担忧也占了上风，但国会回归后可能会重新关注已故性犯罪者的活动
随着美国选民前往投票站参加至关重要且令人担忧的中期选举，杰弗里·爱泼斯坦调查中的一些幸存者的支持者表示担心这起丑闻可能会退居幕后。
然而，政治专家认为，爱泼斯坦问题不会永远消失，许多选民可以在负担能力和人工智能等日常担忧与涉及已故金融家和被指控的性贩运者的丑闻之间取得平衡，后者的社交圈在美国精英中广泛存在。
“我最担心的不是公众会忘记杰弗里·爱泼斯坦，而是负责问责的政客和机构会利用世界事件的混乱作为继续前进的借口，”代表多位爱泼斯坦幸存者的戈德劳公司的斯宾塞·库文说。
库文补充道：“战争、经济危机和政治争议可能占据头条新闻，但它们并不能消除受害者的痛苦，也不能消除有关爱泼斯坦及其强大同伙数十年来如何被允许运作的悬而未决的问题。
“正义不应该有有效期，它当然不应该由新闻周期决定。我们不能仅仅因为今天的头条新闻更紧急，就让爱泼斯坦丑闻成为昨天的新闻。”
爱泼斯坦的律师和会计师被指控在诉讼中“协助和隐瞒”他的罪行
库文呼吁美国政府继续公布爱泼斯坦的文件——许多人称这些文件被排除在所谓的不完整披露之外——并要求国会要求问责。
马什律师事务所 (Marsh Law) 的詹妮弗·弗里曼 (Jennifer Freeman) 表示：“过去一年，人们的注意力从杰弗里·爱泼斯坦身上转移，这令人失望。”她在有关爱泼斯坦性虐待少女的诉讼中代表众多爱泼斯坦幸存者。
然而，弗里曼对幸存者伸张正义的长期前景表示乐观，他说：“虽然公众的注意力可能已经从爱泼斯坦案件上转移，但考虑到选举周期，我相信很快就会再次集中注意力并承担责任。”
弗里曼指出，她正在继续对美国政府提起诉讼，指控其“数十年来在调查和起诉爱泼斯坦方面一再失败”。她还在对他的遗产提起集体诉讼，该诉讼涉及他收集和制作儿童性虐待图像。
政治专家表示，爱泼斯坦受到竞选政客和选民的关注可能会减少，但这可能只是暂时的下降，而不是永久性的下降。
“确实感觉一切都着火了。我认为人们可以同时关心几件事，但直接影响他们生活的事情往往会被优先考虑，”担任“原则第一”代理主任的共和党策略师布列塔尼·马丁内斯说。 “当他们担心汽油价格、生活成本以及政府是否为他们工作时，爱泼斯坦可能会退出当前的对话。
“我不认为这些问题或对答案的需求已经消失；它们只是在争夺注意力。所以我希望在一段时间内听到更少的信息，而不是看到它完全消失。”
“特朗普每天都有一些事情，”布法罗大学政治学系临床副教授肖恩·多纳休说。
对于多纳休来说，时机也起着关键作用。美国国会一直在休会，众议院没有议员，因此没有对爱泼斯坦文件透明度法案拟议的新版本进行任何讨论。这项名为《爱泼斯坦档案透明度法案 II》的法案旨在解决倡导者所说的当前欧洲自由贸易联盟的缺陷，例如缺乏执行机制。
多纳休说：“感觉每当国会重新开会时，这可能会再次成为一个问题，特别是如果民主党正在考虑控制国会的一个或两个参众两院。”
如果民主党如民意调查所示赢得众议院，多纳休预计他们将迅速“让共和党人陷入与爱泼斯坦对峙的境地”。 “民主党人从第一天起就准备开始调查。”

body_en: ICC prosecutor says court making ‘significant progress’ despite US sanctions | International criminal court | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation
ICC prosecutor says court making ‘significant progress’ despite US sanctions
Nazhat Shameem Khan claims some staff are facing ‘banking difficulties’ but their work is unaffected
The deputy prosecutor of the international criminal court has said that new US sanctions are already beginning to take effect on its staff but insisted they have not hindered the court’s work.

US secretary of state Marco Rubio announced the sanctions earlier this month , accusing the ICC – a frequent Trump administration target – of being a “rogue court” and declaring: “Either the ICC will end its threats, or we will end the ICC.”
Nazhat Shameem Khan – who is co-running the office pending the appointment of a new chief prosecutor – said the court was so far continuing its work.

She said that the Gaza war investigation and others had made “significant progress” since war crimes arrest warrants were issued in November 2024 for Benjamin Netanyahu and the former Israeli defence minister, Yoav Galant. Further applications from the prosecutor were being kept secret by order of the court, she said.

Some ICC staff had however encountered banking problems, she said, even though the US sanctions on the court are not due to take effect until six months from 9 October, the date of their announcement. She said the banks were “over complying” to minimise risk while there is uncertainty over the ultimate scope of the measures.

“These are sanctions imposed on the institutions and in principle, our individual members should not be impacted directly,” the Fijian deputy prosecutor said in an interview with the Guardian. “But again, what I am hearing from members of our staff is that some of them are experiencing difficulties in banking.”

The court is meanwhile working on insulating itself from sanctions imposed by a hostile administration in Washington. It has switched its software from Microsoft to European ​alternatives, and is negotiating with relevant service providers over banking and health insurance.

“All the investigations across all situations continue. We haven’t made any decision based on the sanctions to reduce our capability or reduce our output,” Khan said, acknowledging that it was impossible to anticipate the full impact of sanctions when they officially take effect.

The new US sanctions target the whole institution of the ICC, but the US first targeted 13 ICC staff in February 2025. Khan was one of them, so is accustomed to dealing with sanctions, which affect aspects of everyday life such as banking and insurance.

“Life without a credit card is inconvenient. It’s amazing how many things now we cannot do around the world, particularly in relation to travel, without a credit card,” she said, but added that her inconvenience is put into perspective when she visits refugee camps or sites of mass atrocities.
“We see the faces of our victims for whom sanctions and credit cards are completely irrelevant. They just want justice.”

American sanctions are not the only disruption to the ICC prosecutors’ work. Formal investigations began in late November 2024 into allegations of sexual harassment against the former chief prosecutor, Karim Khan. The British jurist (who is no relation to the deputy prosecutor) denied the charges. He was removed in July this year after a vote by member states.

No further charges over the Gaza war have been announced since late 2024. Khan insisted that investigative work on the Israel-Palestine file has only gone dark because of the court’s ruling earlier this year that all charges and applications for warrants should be kept secret until the judges decide they can be made public.

“Even if we reach a stage of the investigations where it might be imminent, we may not discuss it publicly,” she said. “And so while there might be an appearance that nothing is happening, I can assure you that there’s significant progress in that particular situation as well as others.”

Announcing the sanctions, Rubio gave the ICC a six-month grace period “to negotiate and present a solution to address our concerns” but it is unclear what would satisfy the Trump administration which has exhibited a longstanding hostility towards the court.
Rubio claimed without evidence earlier this month that “globalist ‘experts’ an ocean away” wanted the ICC to prosecute American citizens. Khan said it was unclear who and what Rubio had in mind.

“It is possible that there is, that is a mistaken belief on the part of those who are concerned that we are pursuing Americans, but we certainly haven’t brought any Americans before the court,” she said. “If his reference is to Afghanistan, then in fact the priority for the investigation is in relation to offences committed specifically against women, girls and other vulnerable groups by the Taliban and by the Islamic State Khorasan in Afghanistan.”

国际刑事法院检察官表示，尽管美国制裁，法院仍取得“重大进展”
Nazhat Shameem Khan 声称一些员工面临“银行业务困难”，但他们的工作并未受到影响
国际刑事法院副检察官表示，美国新的制裁措施已经开始对其工作人员生效，但坚称这些制裁并没有妨碍法院的工作。
美国国务卿马可·卢比奥本月早些时候宣布了制裁措施，指责国际刑事法院——特朗普政府经常针对的目标——是一个“流氓法院”，并宣称：“要么国际刑事法院结束其威胁，要么我们将结束国际刑事法院。”
纳扎特·沙米姆·汗 (Nazhat Shameem Khan) 正在等待任命新的首席检察官，他表示，法院目前仍在继续其工作。
她表示，自 2024 年 11 月向本杰明·内塔尼亚胡和以色列前国防部长约阿夫·加兰特发出战争罪逮捕令以来，加沙战争调查和其他调查已取得“重大进展”。她说，根据法院的命令，检察官的进一步申请将被保密。
她表示，尽管美国对国际刑事法院的制裁要到 10 月 9 日（即制裁宣布之日）六个月后才会生效，但一些国际刑事法院工作人员还是遇到了银行业务问题。她表示，银行为了最大限度地降低风险而“过度遵守”，而这些措施的最终范围存在不确定性。
“这些是对机构实施的制裁，原则上，我们的个人成员不应受到直接影响，”斐济副检察官在接受《卫报》采访时表示。 “但我再次从我们的员工那里听到的是，他们中的一些人在银行业遇到了困难。”
与此同时，法院正在努力避免受到华盛顿敌对政府实施的制裁。它已将其软件从微软转向欧洲替代品，并正在与相关服务提供商就银行和健康保险进行谈判。
“针对所有情况的所有调查仍在继续。我们尚未根据制裁做出任何降低我们能力或减少产量的决定，”汗说，他承认不可能预测制裁正式生效后的全面影响。
美国的新制裁针对的是国际刑事法院的整个机构，但美国在2025年2月首次针对了国际刑事法院的13名工作人员。汗就是其中之一，因此习惯于应对制裁，制裁影响到银行和保险等日常生活的各个方面。
“没有信用卡的生活很不方便。令人惊讶的是，现在我们在世界各地有很多事情无法在没有信用卡的情况下做，特别是与旅行有关的事情，”她说，但她补充说，当她访问难民营或大规模暴行地点时，她会考虑到她的不便。
“我们看到受害者的面孔，制裁和信用卡对他们来说完全无关。他们只是想要正义。”
美国的制裁并不是对国际刑事法院检察官工作的唯一干扰。对前首席检察官卡里姆·汗 (Karim Khan) 的性骚扰指控于 2024 年 11 月下旬开始正式调查。英国法学家（与副检察官没有关系）否认了这些指控。经过成员国投票后，他于今年7月被免职。
自 2024 年底以来，没有宣布任何关于加沙战争的进一步指控。汗坚称，以色列-巴勒斯坦档案的调查工作之所以陷入黑暗，是因为法院今年早些时候裁定，所有指控和逮捕令申请都应保密，直到法官决定可以公开。
“即使我们的调查已经进入迫在眉睫的阶段，我们也可能不会公开讨论，”她说。 “因此，虽然表面上似乎什么也没发生，但我可以向你保证，在这种特定情况以及其他情况下都取得了重大进展。”
宣布制裁后，卢比奥给了国际刑事法院六个月的宽限期，“进行谈判并提出解决方案来解决我们的担忧”，但目前尚不清楚什么能让特朗普政府满意，因为特朗普政府长期以来对国际刑事法院表现出敌意。
卢比奥本月早些时候在没有证据的情况下声称，“远隔重洋的全球主义‘专家’”希望国际刑事法院起诉美国公民。汗表示，目前尚不清楚卢比奥的想法是谁以及他想做什么。
她说：“那些担心我们正在追捕美国人的人可能存在错误的信念，但我们肯定没有将任何美国人带上法庭。” “如果他指的是阿富汗，那么实际上调查的重点是塔利班和伊斯兰国呼罗珊组织在阿富汗专门针对妇女、女孩和其他弱势群体实施的犯罪行为。”

body_en: Medical experts shocked by Tennessee team’s ‘malpractice’ in Christa Pike’s failed execution | Christa Pike | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation
Medical experts shocked by Tennessee team’s ‘malpractice’ in Christa Pike’s failed execution
New details of IV team’s attempts to find a vein shared by Pike’s lawyer ‘shocked and disturbed’ practitioners

Medical experts have expressed shock at the apparent incompetence shown by Tennessee’s execution team during the failed lethal injection of Christa Pike , the prisoner who survived a normally fatal dose of pentobarbital, which they say would be considered medical malpractice in any other setting.

New details emerged on Thursday of how Tennessee’s intravenous (IV) team struggled for almost an hour to set up a line into Pike’s arms through which she would be administered the fatal dose of sedative. A blow-by-blow account was released in legal proceedings from Pike’s lawyer, Randy Spivey, who was present inside the death chamber at her 30 September failed execution.

The technical procedures attempted by the four unidentified members of the IV team as they tried to find a vein, as described by Spivey , provoked alarm among medical experts. They said the standards applied appeared to fall glaringly short of anything that would be deemed acceptable in a medical environment.
Christa Pike’s IV team warned vein might be ‘blowing’ before failed execution

“I’m shocked and disturbed by what happened inside the death chamber,” said Jonathan Groner, emeritus professor of clinical surgery at Ohio State University and an expert in execution methods. “The level of incompetence is astounding, and difficult to comprehend.”

Groner, who has written an upcoming book The Hippocratic Paradox that explores the ethical contradictions involved in lethal injections, said that Spivey’s detailed chronology painted a picture in which nobody was in charge and there was no plan in sight.

“What they did to Christa Pike would have been malpractice in a clinical situation. Nobody would infuse a drug like pentobarbital that’s known to cause burns if they were unsure that the IV was actually in place.”

Groner pointed out that the label on a vial of pentobarbital instructs that infusion should cease immediately if the patient complains of pain. Spivey’s account records multiple times in which Pike “grimaced” and said her arm was “really burning”.

Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of a classmate, Colleen Slemmer, when she was 18. Following the failed execution, she spent several days on a ventilator and her lawyers assumed she was brain-dead.
After 10 days in hospital she was returned to her prison cell. She can now talk and walk, but her long-term prospects are not known.

The gruesome nature of Pike’s experiences in the death chamber, which some have likened to torture, have prompted a reckoning on the death penalty nationwide. Tennessee has called off all executions, pending a review.

In Spivey’s detailed account, the IV team used about 10 needles as they repeatedly poked Pike’s arms, failing to secure a line. At several points, team members worried that her veins might have “blown”.

Joel Zivot, a professor of anesthesiology and surgery based in Atlanta, Georgia, who gave expert testimony at legal hearings ahead of Pike’s failed execution, said that the new chronology pointed to several areas of serious concern. “Here we have a poorly written protocol, no one in charge, technology that they may not have had permission to use, and catheters that are far too small for the purpose. We could go on and on …”

Pike’s lawyers, partly on the basis of Zivot’s expert opinion, warned the state on several occasions before the failed execution attempt that the prisoner had exceptionally small and compromised veins.

The Spivey timeline records that at 7.05pm on the evening of the failed execution, about half an hour into the procedure, a member of the IV team asked for a 24-gauge needle “and moved that needle around a lot. Christa continued to grimace.”
Zivot said that a 24-gauge catheter was very small. “That’s the kind of catheter you put in a baby, or a small child.”

He added there was “no way that you can push a 50cc syringe into that small little catheter without it blowing up the vein”. Under Tennessee’s protocol, 50cc of pentobarbital were to be injected into each of Pike’s arms, giving a massive total dose of 5g of the sedative.

医学专家对田纳西州团队在克里斯塔·派克处决失败中的“渎职”感到震惊
IV 团队试图寻找派克律师共有静脉的新细节令从业者“震惊和不安”
医学专家对田纳西州执行小组在对克里斯塔·派克（Christa Pike）注射死刑失败的过程中表现出的明显无能表示震惊。克里斯塔·派克是在通常致命剂量的戊巴比妥中幸存下来的，他们说，在任何其他情况下，这都会被视为医疗事故。
周四公布的新细节显示，田纳西州的静脉注射 (IV) 团队如何奋力近一个小时，在派克的手臂上架起一条线，通过这条线给她注射致命剂量的镇静剂。派克的律师兰迪·斯皮维 (Randy Spivey) 在法律诉讼中公布了详细的叙述，9 月 30 日派克被处决失败时，他在死刑室里。
正如斯皮维所描述的那样，静脉注射小组的四名身份不明的成员在试图寻找静脉时所尝试的技术程序引起了医学专家的警惕。他们表示，所采用的标准似乎明显低于医疗环境中可接受的标准。
克里斯塔·派克（Christa Pike）的 IV 团队在执行失败之前警告说，静脉可能会“破裂”
“我对死刑室内发生的事情感到震惊和不安，”俄亥俄州立大学临床外科名誉教授、执行方法专家乔纳森·格罗纳说。 “无能的程度令人震惊，而且难以理解。”
格罗纳即将出版一本新书《希波克拉底悖论》，该书探讨了注射死刑所涉及的伦理矛盾。格罗纳说，斯皮维详细的年表描绘了一幅没有人负责、也没有任何计划的画面。
“他们对克里斯塔·派克所做的事情在临床情况下属于医疗事故。如果他们不确定静脉注射是否确实到位，没有人会注射戊巴比妥等已知会导致烧伤的药物。”
格罗纳指出，戊巴比妥小瓶上的标签指示，如果患者抱怨疼痛，应立即停止输注。斯皮维的账户多次记录派克“做鬼脸”并说她的手臂“真的在燃烧”。
派克因 1995 年谋杀同学科琳·斯莱默 (Colleen Slemmer) 而被判处死刑，当时她年仅 18 岁。处决失败后，她在呼吸机上度过了几天，她的律师认为她已经脑死亡。
住院十天后，她被送回牢房。她现在可以说话和走路，但她的长期前景尚不清楚。
派克在死刑室的经历令人毛骨悚然，有些人将其比作酷刑，这促使全国范围内对死刑进行了反思。田纳西州已取消所有处决，等待审查。
在 Spivey 的详细描述中，IV 团队使用了大约 10 根针，反复戳 Pike 的手臂，但未能固定住一根线。有几次，团队成员担心她的静脉可能“爆裂”。
佐治亚州亚特兰大的麻醉学和外科教授乔尔·齐沃特 (Joel Zivot) 在派克被处决失败之前的法律听证会上提供了专家证词，他表示，新的年表指出了几个值得严重关注的领域。 “我们的方案写得很糟糕，没有人负责，他们可能没有获得使用许可的技术，而且导管对于该目的来说太小了。我们可以继续下去……”
派克的律师在部分基于齐沃特的专家意见的基础上，在执行死刑失败之前多次警告州政府，这名囚犯的静脉异常细小且受损。
斯皮维的时间线记录了，在执行失败当晚的晚上 7 点 05 分，也就是手术进行了大约半小时后，IV 团队的一名成员要求使用 24 号针头，“并把针头移动了很多次。克里斯塔继续做鬼脸。”
Zivot 说 24 号导管非常小。 “这就是你放入婴儿或小孩体内的那种导管。”
他补充说，“你不可能将 50cc 的注射器推入那根小小的导管而不炸毁静脉”。根据田纳西州的方案，派克的每只手臂都要注射 50cc 戊巴比妥，总剂量为 5 克。

Russia steps up election influence efforts in final stretch of midterms

A pedestrian looks at his smartphone on an embankment with the Kremlin in the background in central Moscow on Oct. 8, 2026. Researchers who track online influence operations say Kremlin-backed groups are renewing tactics they've used to sow distrust and discord in previous elections in the U.S. and around the world. Igor Ivanko/AFP via Getty Images hide caption

Russian operatives are pumping out fabricated claims about Democratic candidates, AI-manipulated videos of celebrities and fake posts impersonating real news outlets in an effort to influence American voters in the final run-up to Election Day.

Researchers who track online influence operations and lawmakers who've been briefed by the intelligence community say Kremlin-backed groups are renewing familiar tactics they've used to sow distrust and discord in previous elections in the U.S. and around the world.
Top 2 Democrats on Intel say they're preparing for Trump to claim foreign meddling

"It's a carnival out there," Rep. Jim Himes of Connecticut , the ranking member on the House intelligence committee, told reporters this week. "They're throwing everything out there to generate a sense of chaos and anarchy."
The goal is to exacerbate divisions, erode confidence in democracy and, crucially, undermine U.S. support for Ukraine.

"At the end of the day, the main issue for Russia is and has to be Ukraine," said Darren Linvill, co-director of Clemson University's Media Forensics Hub, who has tracked foreign propaganda campaigns for years.

Linvill says the Russian playbook is consistent. A false claim or divisive narrative is seeded on social media or on a fake website posing as a news organization or think tank. It's spread by state media, automated fake accounts or, increasingly, paid influencers, in the hopes that it gets seen and repeated by real people.

"In the same way that marketing companies will pay an influencer to disseminate, you know, 'Nike's a great shoe,' the Russians do it with false information and made-up lies," he said. "They use influencers that know their audience, that are part of that audience, and they know how to give that audience a message that they want to hear," Linvill said.
A Russian operation put that playbook to work this week to spread a baseless accusation against a Democratic U.S. Senate candidate.

Linvill and several other research groups attributed them to Russian operators the research community has dubbed Storm-1516 . It's known for staging fake videos with actors and laundering their claims through influencer accounts with large followings.

Two fraudulent videos targeting the Senate candidate were posted on Tuesday on X by an account created last month that had few followers. The account's X profile said it was based in the U.S. but the social media platform publicly flagged it as possibly using a proxy such as a virtual private network, which could disguise its location.
OpenAI caught Russians and Iranians using ChatGPT for influence campaigns

The videos were likely created using artificial intelligence, according to Graphika, a research company that analyzes online communities. Linvill said a hallmark of Storm-1516 videos is the use of real actors whose faces are swapped using AI to look like someone else.

英特尔的两名顶级民主党人表示，他们正在为特朗普声称外国干预做准备
“这是一场狂欢节，”众议院情报委员会高级成员、康涅狄格州众议员吉姆·海姆斯本周对记者说。 “他们把一切都扔在那里，以产生混乱和无政府状态的感觉。”
其目标是加剧分歧，削弱对民主的信心，最重要的是，削弱美国对乌克兰的支持。
“归根结底，俄罗斯的主要问题是而且必须是乌克兰，”多年来一直跟踪外国宣传活动的克莱姆森大学媒体取证中心联席主任达伦·林维尔说。
林维尔表示，俄罗斯的战术是一致的。虚假主张或分裂性叙述散布在社交媒体或冒充新闻机构或智囊团的虚假网站上。它通过官方媒体、自动虚假账户或越来越多的付费影响者传播，希望它能被真实的人看到和重复。
“就像营销公司花钱请有影响力的人来传播‘耐克是一双很棒的鞋’一样，俄罗斯人也用虚假信息和编造的谎言来传播，”他说。林维尔说：“他们使用的影响者了解他们的受众，他们是受众的一部分，他们知道如何向受众传达他们想听到的信息。”
俄罗斯的一项行动本周将这一策略付诸实施，散布针对美国民主党参议员候选人的毫无根据的指控。

body_en: ‘It was so magical’: the 33-year-old who made history swimming the length of California | California | The Guardian Skip to main content Skip to navigation
‘It was so magical’: the 33-year-old who made history swimming the length of California
Ultra-endurance swimmer Catherine Breed navigated waves, wildlife and pollution to become the first person to swim from state’s northern-most tip to Mexico border

N early four months ago, Catherine Breed, a 33-year-old from the San Francisco Bay Area, set out to become the first person to swim the entire coastline of California – from its northern-most tip to the border with Mexico. She and her support team prepared for encounters with sharks and storms. They hadn’t anticipated completing the marathon swim during a year of historic super El Niño weather .
But after dodging hurricanes, wildlife and 8ft waves in an unusually volatile Pacific Ocean, Breed finally celebrated the end of her journey on a beach in San Diego on Monday.

Breed joins a group of elite ultra-endurance swimmers who continue to set new records for long-distance swims, including swimming the entire coastlines of Ireland and Iceland and one side of New Zealand’s North Island – all journeys of close to 1,000 miles (1,600km).

Breed spoke to the Guardian this week about living onboard the Catalyst, the sailboat that accompanied her, her physical and mental preparations for her 111-day swim, and what she thought about while spending more than 15 weeks in the water. The conversation has been edited for length and clarity.
On your website , you talk about the desire to be part of “an elite group of humans who have been the first to accomplish a monumental feat ”. What does that feel like now that you’ve done it?

It is a little bit of an out-of-body experience. Like, I know I’m the one who did it, but there are parts of me where I feel like I’m along with the audience, watching this thing happen. I think I’m still trying to grasp what I’ve done.
How did you get the idea to swim the full length of California , which no one has ever done before?

Other people showed me that the model was possible. Ross Edgley swam around Great Britain . Sean Conway and Jasmine Harrison swam the length of Britain. [In 2022] I did a swim down the California coast from the Golden Gate Bridge to Half Moon Bay, and it made me realize how much fun I had during that, and I was like: I want to try to do this with the coast.
What did you think about while you were swimming four to five hours a day?

In college, my coach used to say you only get so many energy units per day. Overthinking or excessive thinking or negative thinking – that can take some of that energy you have. During these marathon swims, I try to keep my thoughts very focused on the task at hand. Coaching myself to get to the next 30 minutes, coaching myself to do the next 2 miles, and kind of like celebrating those little moments. When the conditions were really rough, there was a lot of thought around my technique, because I really had to adjust how I was swimming to not wreck my shoulders in the big waves.

I had earplugs on, so I couldn’t hear the crew. But one thing I could hear very clearly was dolphins. And so there were many occasions where I would hear the dolphins before the crew could see them. And I would look up and I’d be like, you guys, incoming, there’s dolphins.
At points, you were swimming through 6-8ft waves, which you have described as feeling like you were in a washing machine. What is it like to swim in those conditions?

If I’m swimming into the swell, it feels like you’re swimming up a hill. But if it’s behind me, then it’s actually very fun because it feels like I’m surfing. So it really depended on the conditions. When you’ve got a lot of wind and a lot of swell, the waves can crash on you from the back or the side or the front. And it does take a lot of effort to keep my body in the right position. One day a wave picked me up, and I landed on my butt.
How do you train for swimming in those kinds of waves?

I’ve been marathon swimming for 10 years. I grew up swimming, I grew up sailing. So my whole life has been in the ocean. So those moments, they’re difficult, but I’m comfortable. I surf a lot. And so I think surfers are comfortable with waves and they understand kind of just wave mechanics and moving with the ocean.

I think the challenging part of the swell was not so much as swimming, but that there’s no chance of recovery [with living on a boat]. Getting ready to swim is really hard – like you’re trying to make breakfast and you’re falling over, your coffee’s spilling. Even putting my wetsuit on is a challenge in itself.
Were there days when you woke up and did not want to get in the water?

“这太神奇了”：33 岁的游泳者游遍加州创造了历史
超耐力游泳运动员凯瑟琳·布里德 (Catherine Breed) 克服海浪、野生动物和污染，成为从该州最北端游到墨西哥边境的第一人
四月初，来自旧金山湾区的 33 岁凯瑟琳·布里德 (Catherine Breed) 出发，成为第一个游遍加州整个海岸线的人——从最北端到墨西哥边境。她和她的支持团队为遭遇鲨鱼和风暴做好了准备。他们没想到在历史性的超级厄尔尼诺天气的一年里完成了马拉松游泳比赛。
但在异常波动的太平洋中躲避飓风、野生动物和 8 英尺高的海浪后，布里德终于于周一在圣地亚哥的海滩上庆祝了她的旅程的结束。
布里德加入了一群精英超耐力游泳运动员的行列，他们不断创造长距离游泳的新纪录，包括游遍爱尔兰和冰岛的整个海岸线以及新西兰北岛的一侧，所有行程都接近 1,000 英里（1,600 公里）。
布里德本周向《卫报》讲述了她在陪伴她的帆船 Catalyst 上的生活、她为 111 天游泳所做的身心准备，以及她在水中度过超过 15 周的时间的想法。为了长度和清晰度，对话已被编辑。
在您的网站上，您谈到了成为“人类精英团体中的一员的愿望，他们是第一个完成伟大壮举的人”。现在你已经做到了，感觉如何？
这是一种有点灵魂出窍的体验。就像，我知道我是做这件事的人，但我的某些部分感觉我和观众在一起，看着这件事发生。我想我仍在努力理解我所做的事情。
你是怎么想到要游遍整个加利福尼亚州的呢？以前从来没有人做过这样的事？
其他人向我表明该模型是可行的。罗斯·埃德格利游遍了英国。肖恩·康威和茉莉花·哈里森游遍了英国。 [2022 年] 我沿着加州海岸从金门大桥游到了半月湾，这让我意识到在那段时间我有多么有趣，我当时想：我想尝试在海岸上这样做。
当你每天游泳四到五个小时时，你在想什么？
在大学里，我的教练曾经说过，你每天只能获得这么多的能量单位。过度思考或过度思考或消极思考——这可能会消耗你的一些能量。在这些马拉松游泳过程中，我努力让自己的注意力集中在手头的任务上。训练自己完成接下来的 30 分钟，训练自己完成接下来的 2 英里，有点像庆祝那些小时刻。当条件非常恶劣时，我对自己的技术进行了很多思考，因为我确实必须调整自己的游泳方式，以免在大浪中伤到肩膀。
我戴着耳塞，所以听不到工作人员的声音。但我能听得很清楚的一件事是海豚。因此，很多时候我会在船员看到海豚之前就听到它们的声音。我抬头一看，就会说，你们来了，有海豚。
有时，您游过 6 至 8 英尺的海浪，您形容感觉就像在洗衣机里一样。在这样的条件下游泳是什么感觉？
如果我游进海浪中，感觉就像你游上一座小山。但如果它在我身后，那实际上非常有趣，因为感觉就像我在冲浪。所以这确实取决于条件。当风很大且浪很大时，海浪可能会从后面、侧面或前面冲击到您。而且确实需要付出很大的努力才能让我的身体保持在正确的位置。有一天，一个海浪把我卷起，我屁股着地。
如何训练在这种海浪中游泳？
我参加马拉松游泳已有10年了。我从小就游泳，我从小就航海。所以我的一生都在海洋里。所以那些时刻，虽然很困难，但我很舒服。我经常冲浪。所以我认为冲浪者对波浪感到舒服，他们了解波浪力学和随海洋移动。
我认为海浪的挑战并不在于游泳，而是没有恢复的机会（住在船上）。准备游泳真的很困难——就像你在准备早餐时摔倒了，咖啡也洒了一样。甚至穿上潜水衣本身就是一个挑战。
是否有过几天你醒来后不想下水？
